marrow__PHYSIO_CH39_Q019.takeaway: Adrenal androgen excess, especially DHEA/DHEA-S, can cause virilization and hirsutism in a female patient.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH39_Q019.displayText:
Adrenal androgen excess, especially DHEA/DHEA-S, can cause virilization and hirsutism in a female patient.

Hirsutism and masculinization in a female suggest excessive androgens like dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA).

Adrenogenital syndrome is due to an adrenocortical tumor secreting excessive quantities of androgens that cause intense masculinizing effects. In boys, it presents as precocious puberty. In women, virile characteristics develop, including:
• Growth of a beard.
• Deeper voice.
• Masculine distribution of hair on the body and the pubis and
• Growth of the clitoris.

The excretion of 17-ketosteroids (which are derived from androgens) in the urine may be 10 to 15 times elevated. This finding can be used in diagnosing the disease.
emphasis: Adrenal androgen excess, especially DHEA/DHEA-S, can cause virilization and hirsutism in a female patient

rationales.b: Aldosterone excess causes mineralocorticoid effects rather than virilization.
rationales.c: Cortisol excess causes Cushingoid features, not androgenic masculinization.
rationales.d: Epinephrine is a catecholamine and does not cause androgenic changes.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH39_Q020.takeaway: ACTH stimulates adrenal cortex steroidogenesis but does not directly regulate medullary epinephrine secretion.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH39_Q020.displayText:
ACTH stimulates adrenal cortex steroidogenesis but does not directly regulate medullary epinephrine secretion.

The secretion of the adrenal medullary hormones (epinephrine, norepinephrine, and dopamine) is not controlled directly by ACTH.
emphasis: ACTH stimulates adrenal cortex steroidogenesis but does not directly regulate medullary epinephrine secretion

rationales.a: ACTH supports glucocorticoid synthesis in zona fasciculata.
rationales.b: ACTH stimulates adrenal androgen synthesis from zona reticularis.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH39_Q021.takeaway: DHEA-S is produced by the adrenal gland and is not secreted by female ovaries, unlike ovarian sex steroids.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH39_Q021.displayText:
DHEA-S is produced by the adrenal gland and is not secreted by female ovaries, unlike ovarian sex steroids.

DHEAS is exclusively secreted from the adrenals but not by ovaries because ovaries lack the enzyme dehydroepiandrosterone-sulphotransferase needed to form DHEAS.

90% of DHEA is synthesised by the adrenals and 10% comes from the ovaries.
emphasis: DHEA-S is produced by the adrenal gland and is not secreted by female ovaries, unlike ovarian sex steroids

rationales.a: Ovaries produce progesterone, especially from corpus luteum.
rationales.b: DHEA can be produced by both adrenal and ovarian tissue.
